title: The scalar counit equation for the transported composite chart
statement:
Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. All schemes are separated of finite type over $k$, and all maps are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a unital homomorphism of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$, and choose $N=\ell^n\geq1$ annihilating both. On either the ordinary etale or pro-etale site let $\mathcal C_{T,R}=D^b_{ctf}(T,R)$ mean the full category of constant-$R$ module complexes with bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude: tensor with any degree-zero module sheaf has cohomology in one fixed finite interval [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude, det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer]. Write $T_T=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The finite Tate line is $R_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}R_T$ on the etale site and its comparison inverse image on the pro-etale site; $(d)$ denotes tensor with its $d$th tensor power [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist].
Let $e:U\to\mathbf A^d_Y$ be separated etale of finite type, $g=p_de$, and choose standing compactifications. Use $F^{et}_{g,R}\dashv H^{et}_{g,R}$ and $F^{pro}_{g,R}\dashv H^{pro}_{g,R}$ with their specified sum-then-ordered-affine counits as constructed in [lem-sp-chart-finite-ring-adjunction], for $R=A,B$. On either site the natural isomorphism
$$a_{g,K}:T_UH_{g,A}K\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{g,B}T_YK$$
is the canonical derived tensor/pullback, shift and Tate identification [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback, det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]; on the Tate line it sends $(z\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $z\otimes\varphi(a)b$. Let $\beta_g$ on the etale site and $b_g$ on the pro-etale site be the specified compact-support coefficient maps [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility]. For every $K\in\mathcal C_{Y,A}$, the actual composite chart counits satisfy
$$\epsilon^{et}_{g,B,T_YK}\circ F^{et}_{g,B}(a_{g,K})\circ\beta_g(H^{et}_{g,A}K)=T_Y(\epsilon^{et}_{g,A,K}),$$
and
$$\widetilde\epsilon_{g,B,T_YK}\circ F^{pro}_{g,B}(a_{g,K})\circ b_g(H^{pro}_{g,A}K)=T_Y(\widetilde\epsilon_{g,A,K}).$$
These equations use the specified fixed-compactification maps and remain true after canonical refinement identifications. They concern the explicit chart right functor and its counit, without assuming an exceptional coefficient comparison invertible or choosing any smooth orientation.

proof.text: Construct the coefficient-line record with identity on roots and the generator-normalized ordinary balancing isomorphism. Its derived isomorphism is reductionEtaleTateIso. The shared adjunction-transpose presentation of scalarSingleMap makes its derived normalization the specified canonical map; scalarSingleMap_cochain proves equality to the original localization formula. Induction on the ordered coordinate number identifies coordinateAffineScalarIso with reductionEtaleAffineScalarIso, including the identity when d=0. Conjugating by the exact/derived etale pullback comparison identifies the chart scalar arrow with rawChartScalarIso.

Apply [lem-sp-raw-chart-scalar-counit-pasting] to obtain the raw sum-then-affine scalar equation and the finite-Tor scalar-domain witness. Its exact inverse-image presentation is conjugated to the coordinate presentation by the canonical exact/derived pullback isomorphisms.

The graph-normalized ambient comparison is F_d of the inverse normalized sum comparison followed by etaleCompositor: use the ambient/model identification [lem-sp-chart-normalized-model-identification] and the canonical composition identity [lem-sp-chart-sum-affine-counit-transport]. The sum and composition coefficient squares of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility], after replacing etaleCoefficientMap by the equal natural compactScalarMap [lem-pur-etale-compact-scalar-coherence], give its scalar square. This replacement is elementary naturality and inverse cancellation; it does not require a new normalized left comparison theorem.

Use [lem-sp-affine-compactification-normalization] to identify affineLeftOnPlus with the ambient ordered comparison. Uniqueness of normalized Tate transport and projective-line data identifies the supplied t_R,P_R with the canonical raw-chart data. Datum.etaleCounit [lem-sp-chart-finite-ring-adjunction], naturality of the affine and chart comparisons, and the composite-adjunction counit formula then give the raw counit preceded by the inverse ambient comparison and the exact/derived pullback identification. Move these identifications through the coefficient map by naturality, use the scalar square from the preceding step, and cancel the inverse left comparisons. Apply the raw equation to prove the etale clause. This works for each arbitrary supplied cp and cg; refinement/composition coherence is that of their specified comparisons.

In the pro-etale clause, apply the etale scalar-counit equation to the actual representative J=CA.eY.inverse(K). The scalar-domain theorem puts its scalar extension in the etale and pro-etale finite-Tor domains. Apply the site/coefficient square at HA(J). Naturality of the B compact-support site comparison at the ordered coordinate scalar map and naturality of the scalar/site comparison at the A counit give the conjugated scalar equation. Evaluate the A and B geometric counits using lem-sp-chart-geometric-counit-evaluation, with endpoint isomorphisms aA=CA.eY.counit after CA.heY and aB=deltaY inverse followed by scalar extension of aA. Datum.geometric_normalization cancels the A geometric identification. Naturality of the named pro-etale coefficient map moves that identification through b. The remaining composition is precisely geometricScalarIso; the site diagram identity gives the asserted equation on every K.
